# Validation contract

**Note:** This file was generated by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol under the direction of Adam Phillippy.

This contract defines the validation claims and release gates for development after
v0.2.0. Acceptance limits, fixture identities, and test tiers are fixed before the
corresponding implementation is evaluated. Unfavorable results are retained and cause
the stage to stop for review rather than being removed or silently reclassified.

## Scientific claim

The primary scientific quantity is maximum directed containment of distinct canonical
k-mer sets:

```text
C = max(containment(X core, Y expanded), containment(Y core, X expanded))
ANI_c = C^(1/k)
```

`ANI_c` is the historical ModDotPlot name for the containment-derived display
transform. It is not asserted to be biological average nucleotide identity and is not
interchangeable with alignment-based measures such as `ANI_m`.

The production estimator is accepted only by testing its estimated containment against
containment computed from complete, lossless canonical k-mer sets. Metrics on `ANI_c`
test the quantized product output derived from that same containment oracle; they do
not introduce a biological-ANI claim.

When a biological variable is shown for interpretation, the only planned comparison is
to a controlled point-mutation rate with large indels excluded, following the use made
in Figure 4 of the ModDotPlot paper. Repeats, ambiguity, offsets, inversions, unequal
lengths, and indels may still be input fixtures for estimator robustness, but their
reference remains exact k-mer-set containment, not a biological identity label.

## Fixed v0.2.1 validation target

The browser defaults under test are:

| Tier | Registers | HLL precision | Sparse correction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Preview | 256 | 10 | disabled |
| Detailed | 1,024 | 10 | disabled |

The normal scientific acceptance test must construct and freeze axes through the
production builders, compute complete production tiles, and compare every valid cell
with the exact canonical k-mer-set oracle. It must cover point substitutions, repeat
context, unequal cardinality, missing cells, and forward/reverse direction.

The detailed tier is release-blocking for `ANI_c` error and product-output stability.
The preview tier is release-blocking for missing/present agreement and bounded
structural degradation, but remains explicitly provisional. The final
selective preview/detailed composite is characterized separately. If that
characterization violates its preregistered gate, v0.2.1 stops without silently
changing the scheduler.

For valid cells whose exact `ANI_c` is at least 0.80, the bounded pull-request fixture
uses these deliberately conservative limits:

| Metric | Preview limit | Detailed limit |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Mean absolute `ANI_c` error | 0.050 | 0.010 |
| P95 absolute `ANI_c` error | 0.300 | 0.040 |
| Combined false-positive plus false-negative crossing rate at the 0.80 display floor | 10% of valid cells | 5% of valid cells |

These are fixed-browser-path limits using the production hash seed. The broader
four-layout validation-only sweep permits preview mean absolute `ANI_c` error up to
0.080 because it deliberately includes three perturbed hash layouts; its detailed
mean/P95 and both tiers' P95/crossing limits remain the values above.

Missing/present disagreement and high-support direction-sign errors are zero-tolerance
gates. Crossing rates at 0.85, 0.90, and 0.95 are reported as diagnostics, not treated
as biological categories or release boundaries. The composite characterization permits
mean/P95 disagreement from all-detailed `ANI_c` of 0.030/0.100 over relevant cells, no
new missing cells, and no more than 2% of valid cells crossing the 0.80 display floor.

## Baselines and change control

Before behavior-preserving refactors, retain deterministic fixtures for:

1. Numeric identity, direction, and direction-support channels.
2. Preview, detailed, exact-terminal, self, pairwise, and missing-data paths.
3. Configuration serialization and digests.
4. Renderer transfer-function and direction-confidence behavior.
5. Selective-composite quality choice and output.
6. Exact full-footprint geometry, repeat-rich numerical goldens, full-versus-split
   tile equivalence, and even-k ambiguous-orientation behavior. Internal anchor
   coverage may remain as a core regression even though anchors are not a browser
   display option.
7. Exact integer-texture rendering at fractional CSS widths and device pixel ratios 1
   and 2 without interpolated colors.

Exact byte equality is required for integer numeric channels on the pinned reference
toolchain. Cross-browser screenshots use a declared perceptual tolerance rather than
requiring driver-dependent byte equality.

Any change to numeric tiles, selective-composite membership, or the interpretation of
`ANI_c` requires an explicit contract/version decision and new fixtures. The
scientific-configuration digest identifies tile computation. Scheduler and per-tile
quality provenance are separate product metadata and must not be implied by that
digest.

## Test tiers

| Tier | Purpose | Trigger |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pull request | Bounded deterministic correctness, goldens, parser properties, browser behavior | Every change |
| Scheduled | Multi-realization containment statistics, randomized worker sequences, parser fuzzing | Nightly or explicitly dispatched |
| Release | Reference-host browser performance, annotation scale, memory traces, complete scientific reports | Release candidate |

Performance gates record the browser and host, warmup, repetitions, median and tail
latency, retained application estimates, and observable transient memory. Portable
application estimates are not described as complete browser-process or GPU peaks.

## Product sequence

The completed sequence is v0.2.1 evidence hardening, v0.3.0 core-contract refactoring,
v0.4.0 owned browser jobs and operational scaling, v0.5.0 display-aware scheduling plus
scientific validation and initial export, and v0.6.0 production cleanup plus export
usability. v0.7.0 added bounded multi-sequence plot modes, v0.8.0 added staged launch,
grid-detail return navigation, and discrete ColorBrewer presentation controls, and
v0.8.1 added palette direction, leading Spectral/Viridis groups, and editable classes.
v0.8.2 added responsive control-header containment and a live genomic window-size
translation for the current scientific plot resolution. v0.8.3 made that translation
a single rounded value, corrected reciprocal grid orientation and X/Y ordering, moved
self plots to the bottom-left-to-top-right diagonal, and added shared-axis grid
reordering by pointer or keyboard. v0.8.4 placed every grid cell on the genomic domain
of the longest selected sequence so shorter self and pairwise plots retain their
proportional extents and remain aligned across rows and columns.
v0.2.1 was manually accepted; later stages were authorized to proceed without
pausing, provided every source and static-web checkpoint was retained for ordered
testing. A v1.0.0 release remains explicitly outside this sequence; additional usability
work will precede any stable-release decision.
